problem: The UART description lists only two wires, TX and RX. A student wiring a sensor or a second board will often connect only these two and get no working link, because both ends must also share a 0 V reference.
fix: Say that UART needs TX and RX plus a common ground (GND) between the two devices, in addition to the same baud rate.

problem: The note under 'Linux libraries' is 'gpiozero, smbus'. Both are Python libraries, not Linux system libraries, and placing them below the 'Python / app' layer hides that the app imports them directly.
fix: Rename the layer to 'Python libraries' (gpiozero, smbus2) or merge it with the Python layer and keep 'Linux kernel / drivers' as the layer below.

problem: On some board models the RAM is stacked on top of the SoC package (package-on-package) rather than placed beside it, so the sentence is not true of every Pi.
fix: Write 'RAM is a separate chip beside the SoC on most current models, and stacked on top of it on some compact models'.

problem: 'Reads may clash' is vague. The concrete failure is that both sensors answer in the same address slot, so their replies overlap on SDA and the data is corrupted.
fix: Answer: both sensors respond to the same address, so they drive SDA at the same time and the master reads corrupted data. Fix with an I2C multiplexer, a second bus, or by changing one sensor's address if it supports that.

problem: 'This chapter looks at the board blocks, the Linux system that starts on power-up, and the serial interfaces' is filler of the kind this book avoids; it delays the content.
fix: Delete the sentence and end the lead on the sentence about the Pi sensing, deciding, logging and serving a page while driving LEDs, relays and sensors.
